subject: Post-demo: recommended eval shortlist + decision brief for Equinox POC
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@equinox.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended eval shortlist + action items

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid detail on the latency targets and the hallucination patterns you showed during the demo. Quick recap and the two recommended next steps so we keep momentum for the POC decision: 

TL;DR recommended shortlist (why these three):
- redwood-gemini-8q (8-bit quantized): best latency/cost balance for short conversational flows; strong on factuality in our evals for Equinox prompt set.
- redwood-llama-13b-pt (13B pruned + KV cache optimizations): higher quality on multi-step reasoning, modest latency increase but still within your 250ms median target in our tests.
- redwood-mix-70 (70B distilled): highest quality for high-context summarization, but notably higher token cost and tail latency — recommended only for sections of the pipeline that require deep understanding.

Attachments I included: equinox_benchmarks_20270419.csv (benchmarks: median/95/99 latencies, token cost estimates), prompt_set_v2.txt (the prompt/ground-truth pairs we used), and a draft mutual action plan PDF. 

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm which three flows you want in the POC (chat, summarization, rerank). We recommend all three but we can scope to chat+rerank to start.
2) We run a 48-hour targeted eval against your sample traffic with the two top candidate models (gemini-8q and llama-13b-pt) and produce a short quality delta report.
3) Procurement: if you want pricing guidance for Dedicated or hosted SLA, tell us target monthly token throughput so we can produce a committed-capacity proposal.

Open questions from our side:
- For the chat flow, is 99th percentile latency a hard requirement or a soft goal? (you mentioned 500ms in worst-case vs 250ms median)
- Are there any redlines in your data retention / KMS requirements we should account for in the POC?

If you’re good with the above, I’ll kick off the eval run and loop in Alex on infra configuration.

Best,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0146

Attachments: equinox_benchmarks_20270419.csv (CSV), prompt_set_v2.txt (TXT), mutual_action_plan_EQX-437.pdf (PDF)

From: Samir Patel <samir@equinox.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@equinox.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended eval shortlist + action items

Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap and the files. A few quick items from our side:

1) Flows — we want to run chat + summarization for the POC. Summarization is the priority because it’s the bottleneck for our downstream QA team.
2) Latency — 99th percentile is important for us on chat (we need to guarantee sub-800ms for federated users), but median/95th for summarization is acceptable at higher values. If there’s a config that gives predictable degradation under load, that’s preferable to an occasional huge tail.
3) Procurement — provisional throughput: expect 120M tokens/month during POC peak; production could be 600–800M tokens/month if we proceed. Can you send both hosted and Dedicated indicative pricing? Procurement will also want an SLA add-on price estimate.

Also — Elena asked me to confirm: can you surface hallucination regression checks vs our golden prompt set? We’d like automated alerts if accuracy drops >4% for any evaluation suite.

If you need anything else to start the 48-hour run, let us know.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Equinox AI
samir@equinox.ai

Internal notes — keeping this thread to preserve context before we reply to procurement.

Neha / Alex — quick recommedation matrix I ran after reviewing the attached benchmark CSV: 

- Primary POC pair: redwood-gemini-8q (default) + redwood-llama-13b-pt (fallback). Rationale: gemini-8q hits ~180ms median and ~520ms 99th in our sanitized infra test at 8 concurrent streams; llama-13b-pt gives ~15–20% higher pass@accuracy on the Equinox summarization prompt set and degrades more gracefully with larger context windows.
- Cost modeling: for 120M tokens/month POC, hosted per-token estimate:
  * gemini-8q: ~$0.012 / 1k tokens -> ~$1,440/mo
  * llama-13b-pt: ~$0.028 / 1k tokens -> ~$3,360/mo
  (production 600M tokens scales linearly; include volume discounts for Dedicated)
- Hallucination monitoring: suggest we run the 48-hour sweep with the full prompt_set_v2 and add an automated daily QA job that computes the 4% regression threshold Elena requested; if hit, trigger an email + Slack alert to Equinox sup.
- Risk: redwood-mix-70 should be scoped only as a selective pass (e.g., nightly batch for highest-value summaries) because of cost and tail latency risk.

Action items for us: Alex to stand up the eval infra (can use a hosted test seat and traffic replay). Neha to send the M action plan and pricing ranges to Samir + procurement. I’ll draft an SLA add-on quote to include in the package.

Marissa
Director, Solutions 
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi all —

Appreciate the quick feedback, Samir. Short answers and next steps below: 

1) POC scope confirmed: chat + summarization. We’ll run the 48-hour targeted eval against gemini-8q (primary) and llama-13b-pt (fallback). We’ll include the full prompt_set_v2 and produce: median/95/99 latency, token cost, and a quality-delta report against your golden set.
2) Latency: understood — we’ll include 99th percentile measurements and a degradation profile under concurrency to show predictable behavior. We’ll also include KV cache warmup guidance to avoid the worst tails.
3) Procurement numbers: preliminary hosted indicative ranges and a Dedicated capacity sketch are attached (see pricing rows in the CSV). Marissa is drafting a formal SLA add-on; I’ve cc’d her.
4) Hallucination monitoring: we’ll set up the daily QA job and wire an alert for >4% regression. The evaluation run will also surface per-prompt failure modes so you can triage specific templates.

Mutual action plan: I uploaded a short MAP and a shared folder with the test results. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGhIJkLmNopqR (also in related links).

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Thu): we kick the 48-hour run; Alex will provision infra and pull a 24-hour traffic sample you provided.
- Fri: initial latency/cost artifacts + per-prompt QC sheet.
- Early next week: joint review + procurement conversation to convert to a committed proposal.

If procurement needs an official quote or a PO format, ask them to send the required PO fields and I’ll route to finance.

Thanks — we’ll start the run this afternoon and I’ll ping when results are ready.

Best,
